title: Does giving a Markov chain dwell times or a second-order memory let it fool a webcam-signal detector?
lede: does giving a chain over a person's frames dwell times or second-order memory help? No: semi-Markov and second-order chains (8 or 32 states, own or pooled fit, centre or real-frame emission) are all caught at AUROC 0.999 to 1.000.
summary: The predecessor project's first-order Markov chains over DUX webcam-signal frames were caught at AUROC 1.000. Two fixes it named are tried here: a semi-Markov chain that holds each k-means state for a dwell time drawn from that state's empirical run lengths, and a second-order chain whose next state depends on the last two (backing off to first order for unseen pairs). With 8 or 32 states, fitted on one person's earlier windows or on the other 45 people's, emitting state centres or real frames, all 16 cells are scored at AUROC 0.999 to 1.000 by a boosted-tree detector over 3 seeds, in the population and profile-aware detectors alike. Neither fix reaches the 0.57 to 0.65 of stitching 50-frame real blocks. Stylised: one form-filling context, 46 people, k of 8 and 32 only, empirical dwell times without drift.
